newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to seek a four-month delay in IMF exit.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to seek a four-month delay in IMF exit.

text.p: The Philippines will ask for a four-month extension of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme which is due to expire on June 23, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
"We will ask the IMF for an extension up to end-October because that will be the next congressional adjournment," Singson told reporters.
He said details of the extension were yet to be discussed with the IMF's resident representative David Nellor.
The extension is being sought because of the non-passage of the crucial income tax reform bill which is one of the reforms detailed in the three-year IMF programme.
The programme is the last of a series of IMF programmes entered into by the Philippines since late 1960s.
The Congress failed to pass the bill before it adjourned last week. It is to reconvene in late July.

"We did not want to rush the tax measure just for the sake of rushing it. We also did not want to come up with a half-baked measure, so we decided to just wait," Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said.
The tax bill, which aims to widen the coverage of income tax payers, restructure corporate taxes, and plug loopholes, is expected to yield an additional 18 billion pesos in revenues for the country.
